title: Hybrid networking — VPN, Direct Connect, Transit Gateway, PrivateLink

answers.explanation: Site-to-Site VPN = IPSec over internet, hours to stand up — night-21 Block 1 quick hybrid pattern.
Direct Connect = dedicated private circuit for consistent latency and high bandwidth — not VPN over public internet.
DX primary + Site-to-Site VPN backup to same TGW/VGW is the classic resilient hybrid pair.
Transit Gateway hub-spoke scales multi-account VPCs + on-prem without full mesh peering — Scenario 2 in night-21.
VPC peering is non-transitive — A↔B and B↔C does not route A→C; need A↔C peering or TGW.
PrivateLink consumer interface endpoint to vendor NLB service — Scenario 3; no VPC peering to SaaS.
S3 Gateway VPC endpoint in route table — Night 8/10 pattern; PrivateLink is for third-party published services.
Overlapping CIDR blocks break hybrid routing — redesign on-prem or VPC CIDR before VPN/DX.
DX Gateway + Transit Gateway distributes on-prem routes to many VPCs in the Region.
VPN = IPSec by design; DX is private path not encrypted by default — add VPN over DX when exam requires encryption.
Security groups on Aurora for on-prem CIDR + Lambda SG on 5432 — same Night 16 pattern extended hybrid.
Two VPCs, full private IP mesh, same Region → VPC peering; PrivateLink is for service exposure not arbitrary IP routing.
RAM shares Transit Gateway across accounts for spoke attachments — centralized networking account pattern.
Theory night — three paper diagrams (on-prem hybrid, TGW hub, PrivateLink SaaS) per night-21 Block 2.
Client VPN = remote users on laptops; Site-to-Site VPN = DC/router to AWS, not per-laptop.
